stem:
A biologist wishes to test whether the mean concentration $\mu$, in suitable units, of a certain pollutant in a river is below the permitted level of 0.5. She measures the concentration, $x$, of the pollutant at 50 randomly chosen locations in the river. The results are summarised below.

$$n = 50 \qquad \sum x = 23.0 \qquad \sum x^2 = 13.02$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Carry out a test at the 5% significance level of the null hypothesis $\mu = 0.5$ against the alternative hypothesis $\mu < 0.5$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Later, a similar test is carried out at the 5% significance level using another sample of size 50 and the same hypotheses as before. You should assume that the standard deviation is unchanged.
parts.text: Given that, in fact, the value of $\mu$ is 0.4, find the probability of a Type II error.
